product_one_liner.value: Luciq is an agentic mobile observability platform that helps mobile engineering teams detect, prioritize, and resolve app-performance issues across iOS and Android.
product_one_liner.notes: Luciq describes itself as an agentic mobile observability platform helping mobile engineering teams resolve app-performance issues across iOS and Android.

pricing_page.notes: Luciq has a public page titled “Luciq Pricing” describing pricing that scales with customers.

named_customers.notes: named_customers: Luciq’s company announcement says its platform powers the named top apps listed in the answer. | named_customers.0: The company announcement names DoorDash as an app powered by Luciq. | named_customers.1: The company announcement names T-Mobile as an app powered by Luciq. | named_customers.2: The company announcement names Figma as an app powered by Luciq. | named_customers.3: The company announcement names Decathlon as an app powered by Luciq. | named_customers.4: The company announcement names Verizon as an app powered by Luciq.

employee_band.notes: Y Combinator lists team size as 250, and a separate company profile places Luciq in the 201–500 employee band.

hq_location.notes: hq_city: The company’s announcement identifies San Francisco as its headquarters city. | hq_country: The company’s announcement states that Instabug/Luciq is headquartered in San Francisco, United States.

founded_year.notes: Luciq’s official organization metadata lists its foundingDate as 2013.

eng_blog.notes: Luciq’s Engineering category contains multiple technical posts, including posts about understanding/refactoring a decade of code and ClickHouse storage costs. The author Khaled El Morabea is identified as a Director of Engineering, supporting that engineers write technical posts; this meets the threshold of at least two engineering-focused posts.

public_docs.notes: The public Luciq documentation index links to multiple product guides, setup guides for several SDK platforms, CLI/API references, and integrations.

ai_ml_roles_open.notes: Luciq’s current official openings page lists an Enterprise Account Executive and a Product Engineer (Backend), with no qualifying AI, ML, or data-science title.

model_provider.notes: Luciq’s product FAQ on autonomous resolution says it uses multiple third-party AI models, naming OpenAI and Anthropic as examples.

compliance_certs.notes: compliance_certs: Luciq’s FAQ says it is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001:2022 certified and GDPR compliant; these are the three named items within the requested set. | compliance_certs.0: The FAQ explicitly names SOC 2 Type II certification. | compliance_certs.1: The FAQ explicitly names ISO 27001:2022 certification. | compliance_certs.2: The FAQ states that Luciq is GDPR compliant.

last_funding.notes: funding_stage: The funding profile updated in November 2026 identifies the latest round as a Series B. | funding_date: The current funding history identifies the latest round as announced on May 17, 2022; the requested YYYY-MM date is 2022-05. | funding_amount_usd: The funding profile updated in November 2026 identifies the last round as $46M, and Luciq’s own dated announcement states it raised $46 million.

raised_18mo.notes: The funding history, updated November 6, 2026, says the latest round was the $46M Series B announced May 17, 2022, well before the 18-month window preceding November 9, 2026.

hiring_sdr_ae.notes: The current official openings page lists an Enterprise Account Executive position, which meets the requested sales-role definition.

launched_6mo.notes: Luciq’s changelog records a product update shipped on November 4, 2026, introducing Relevant Moments and Multi-Session Summary in Session Replay, inside the six-month window.

leadership_change_12mo.notes: Luciq announced that Greg Meyer joined as CFO, and the announcement’s publication metadata dates it July 22, 2026, within the twelve months preceding November 9, 2026.
